content.label:
You cost more than spotify.  I get the idea behind your app.  It's a good idea and it could probably make you some decent cash if you renamed the app to something more original and rethought how you go about making money.

The fact of the matter is, this app is going to stay hidden from the public until those two issues are addressed.  No one in their right mind is going to pay more than they would pay for something infinitely more useful such as Pandora or Spotify.  Each of those programs have music playlists that is catered to individuals who need to focus.  

The fact that yours is developed by neuroscientists doesn't really matter.  It's like boasting that your app plays all music as lossless FLAC.  Nobody cares about that.  They only care if it works. The only way you can expect the prices you're charging is if what you're offering was unique, but it's not.  I can pay 5$ a month and get playlists to study to yet I can also listen to every single album from all of my favorite artists.

This is coming from someone who makes decent money.  I'm not hurting for cash.  I'm just not careless with it either.

Love the music, love the science, love the concept. 

The app simply does not work. How can too get flow when it stops, crashes, and fails to load. Seriously this is embarrassingly bad.

This is an incredible tool for those of us with attention issues. The app needs a little tweaking but the tool feels almost too good to be true.  I just finished a two hour plane ride. I used wifi to phone and Bose in ear noise cancellers. Reading a book was a breeze--not a typical experience for me.

Focus@will streams music to help you get in the “zone” and focus. The service itself is fantastic. I’ve been struggling for months to find music I can use to block out ambient distractions in my environment and Focus@will’s Classical streaming station fits the bill. I listen for most of the day, almost every day.

However, the iOS app itself is horrible. It’s buggy: sometimes I have to press the play button 2-3 times before the station starts playing. I also *really* don’t need a “Productivity Tracker” — that’s subjective anyway. Just as I was writing this, I got a “Timeout Error” notification — just another bug...
The app has been unreliable after the last upgrade. Music keeps skipping to the point of being unusable. Works fine from the website.

Great functional prowess - I really enjoy using the app for periods of study and concentration. However, the app is buggy and could use a little work. 

First the app has a poor look and feel. It has not been updated for the new iPhone 6/6+ size despite the new phones being released 6 months ago, and the design in my opinion is rather poor. Secondly the app will occasionally "fail to load" which means you cannot access any audio. I have no idea why this occurs so frequently - usually requires you to force restart the app a few times, even on wifi where the connection is rather good. Finally I would suggest tweaking the productivity factor tracking. This is largely a user input process, but the options are in quartiles and sometimes I am feeling between 75% and 100% focused. I would suggest perhaps seeing how many times the user switches out of the app (answering texts, browsing the web) for a true measure of productivity. 

Those criticisms aside, this is a nice (albeit expensive) app to have. The existing competition is limited.

Revised:
My old review is below. The app has only gotten worse with time, and now they're trying to charge for this bug-ridden mess after a "trial" period (used to be free for basic features; now it's disguised as a freemium app). I can't recommend that anyone pay money for this or support these shifty developers, who consistently ignore user feedback, downplay constant errors, write up fake reviews, and now market a paid app as a "free" one. Avoid. 

Old review:
This app legitimately aids my focus...when it's not distracting me to the point of rage with its crashes and failures to launch. The current version is highly unstable and needs to be fixed before this app is useful again. Freezes indefinitely at the loading screen just about every time.

After 30 days it logs you out, asking for $$$. Not robust enough for the expensive subscription. Was better when there was a limited beta version available. Free alternatives available at music streaming sites.

For the app itself I would probably give 4 stars, however, once the Free Trial runs out you get locked out of the App entirely - hence the 2 star rating.
I feel that the monthly/yearly subscription pricing structure is unreasonable. I like the App, but not at that price. 
I like the App enough that I would probably pay for it, but not on a subscription. I think there needs to be a basic level where you can pay a very minimal once off fee and have access to maybe 1 or 2 channels (preferably you can select  the channels that worked best for you and "lock them in" after the free trial period).
I will be deleting this App now since it is completely useless without a subscription. Shame. :(

I am an engineer, a very busy one. I have too many projects going at the same time and a lot of potential distractions all day long. Finding this service was a huge improvement to my daily work flow. I use the timer a lot so I set focus work sessions for 60 minutes at a time and, unless I am interrupted by a visit or a phone call, I can focus on a single task, get it done, and actually enjoy doing whatever it is. 

It helps make tedious, repetitive crap work easier to get through and it seems to help the creative process for more complicated jobs as well.  

I use it when I am working from home too. It really helps keep the innumerable distractions and diversions from my mind.   

When I am more productive I feel better at the end of the day, I sleep better because I am making good progress on projects.

Try it!

Update: it seems like some of the old bugs with this app are coming back. I usually have to touch the start/play button several times to get it to work, and it is still not cooperating with the base IOS lockout settings. I hope the development team is still working on updates and bug fixes because I would really like to keep using this app.

I really wish I had had this app in grad school. It really does work. The variety of music choices give you options depending on what level of focus you need. They still have a few bugs to work out, notably the inability to engage the lockout from the iOS. However, I highly recommend it regardless.

title.label: Lifesaver! No offline-mode is its only flaw

content.label:
I am at the end of my free trial and–wow!! I have major anxiety and ADHD/ADD. I have so many ideas and it is always a struggle to stick to an idea and develop it (i.e. writing papers). This, along with timers, has really decreased that struggle. I also live with my mother (I am a young adult), who talks out of anxiety incessantly, and I play this when she stifles me with her repetitive ramblings to drown her out and to self-soothe myself. 

What is surprising to me is that normally classical music makes me fidgety, but here I can enjoy its beauty with out anxiety. This really makes me want to research the scientific research behind this app, because whatever they have modified in the classical music works for me (I believe they have modified the classical music, but have yet to do a side-by-side comparison to other sources of the tracks, so this is not definitive). Also, the ADHD mode (the primary mode I use) is music with a fast tempo, which is a surprise for me but has been the key. It lets me ride out the wave of ny anxieties and discursiveness.

With this app, I have access to a retreat in the palm of my hands, in the middle of a squirmy, noisy, lively, icky, golden city; this app is my home-base among this flitting, inconsistent city. And, more profoundly, it overthrows the flitting, inconsistency of my mind normally reigned by rumination and anxiety.

Some unique features: an option among three different intensity modes for each type of music; and a cinematic mode (never thought of this as a possible music genre, but when you hear it you will see that it is mot juste). 

Now, this would get 5 stars ⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ IF it had an offline mode. I live in a huge, noisy city and would love to use this while on the subway, where I spend a good 10% of my out-and-about waking life. 

Thank you focus@will!

Music/Sound is constantly stopping for no reason. I have to repeatedly keep coming back to the app to hit play again. Transitions between screen are slow. The loading spinner is annoying and ugly.

For a focus application, this app is very distracting.
Similar apps range from a one time payment of $.99 to $5.99 which includes free updates for life! This app is $50 a year!!! Huge SCAM to play the same 10 music track over and over.
This app helped me in several ways. I used it while studying for my senior year finals and aced them all. And then it helped me while brainstorming for my own mobile app start up!

title.label: App crashes every time upon opening...

content.label: The App crashes every time upon opening...I was listening to free trial and loved it. So then I went to purchase the app and after doing so, the app crashes every time when I try opening it😕. It's a bummer cause I loved the concept. Hopefully this will be remedied so I can eventually use the app again...

For a while this was free. I paid them for a few months because I liked what they were doing. I didn't think it was a good value so I quit paying. Apparently in the past few months they decided to restrict free play and now the app is completely worthless. It's a bad business model and junk science. I would never pay for this again.

title.label: Seems like a useful app but is still buggy

content.label: I am able to focus more on tasks that I work on, but an app "Time-out" error keeps the app from functioning for more than 20 or 30 minutes at a time which is a bit frustrating.
Love it.  Wish the full version was not so expensive

title.label: Good idea crippled by crappy app wrapper

content.label: Application requires downloading and streaming every track. Not useful when data is not readily available.

title.label: I love this app so much!

content.label: One of my friend was using this app, and app was playing good music so I asked what is the name of app. After I downloaded this, I can focus reading and homework better than don't have this app! I definitely like subscribe!

Kept getting an error that services kept timing out and then it would freeze up on me trying to process the music. Times it would come in and out. Burnt my productivity. Couldn't get it to work but 50% of time. Likes the concept and potential.

title.label: I love it. I miss my music!

content.label: My focus explodes when i use this app.  I love it. Truly do.  That's why this will sound like a back-handed compliment: I love it, but i miss my music!   Let me explain.  I'm most distractible, all else being equal, when I'm NOT listening to any form of music.  Music has always been a part of my work routine...and I LOVE MUSIC.  I like picking out artists that fit my mood, etc...  I listened to a podcast which introduced me to this app and during the podcast they mentioned that its essential to listen to wordless music.  Intrigued, i signed up for the trial.  For my particular version of crazy (yours may be different) this assertion proves absolutely true.  I've tried, because i miss it, to go back to listening to my favorite music while working and i've had to "face the music" (couldn't resist) that i work a lot better with the wordless music provided by this app.  AWESOME work.  Many  thanks.
This would be a 5 star app if it did not randomly stop playing music and then continue to load until you shut it down and start the app again. Please get this fixed.

I love this app, however it is causing more frustration than anything currently as the tracks keep skipping or times out. Having to stop what I'm doing to try and get the app to work defeats the entire purpose of using it! When I'm paying a monthly fee to subscribe I expect it to work. If this spotty service continues, I will discontinue my subscription. When it works it is EXTREEMLY helpful and it assists me in focusing and getting things done at work. Please fix these bugs!!
Room noise eliminator and hyper focus tuner-iner. Dream come true. One of my can't live without apps.
Really delivers on the promise. Focus at Will has completely changed the way I work.

This definitely helps me focus, but the constant stopping and skipping is distracting (which kind if defeats the purpose). This is not inexpensive, so I find this disappointing. Fix this and I'll be happy.
It works!
This is the breakthrough productivity app I was looking for. I get so much more done now.
I use it every day
This actually works. It's an indispensable tool in our noisy world.

This is an awesome app!  It really works. When I need to focus and get some work done, I turn it on and am really able to focus. Although I have ADD, I find that the acoustic version works well for me. I recently purchased the paid version, but really haven't explored the additional venues.

I use this software almost daily for background music while dictating and studying.  It is stimulating without being distracting...I paid for the yr- well worth the cost of a latte each month for something I use several days weekly.  Would like to see more tunes added to cinematic...

I could not sign up via Facebook no matter how much I tried, even after reinstalling and resetting the app's access in FB. The spinner just get spinning. None of my other apps has a problem with FB authentication, so I don't think it's my iPad. I finally got set up through my google+ account. The developer might want to check on this since the app was just featured in Mashable. Once it finally launched, I found the music pleasing (aside from ADHD beta). I can see this app being beneficial for concentration. A couple things that might inspire user confidence: can't the picture be hi def, or is that a paid option? And how about more frequent updates? September 2013 was a long time ago.

title.label: Music stops playing all the time

content.label:
The music seems to work but the app doesn't.

The music randomly stops playing and you have to restart it. It's very very annoying. 

I quickly stopped using it. 

It should have been fixed by now.
This has helped me focus at work, though I wish the app would be fixed up a bit. It freezes and shuts down often.

title.label: Great concept, functionality still needs work

content.label: I purchased the Pro version about six week ago and noticed right away that the program froze and stopped playing songs after 5 minutes or so, forcing me to manually tap the "stop" button and then re-start, which totally disrupts my focus. Contacted customer service, they were friendly and did their best to resolve the issues, but ultimately had to cancel my Pro subscription. I love concept, and will definitely try the app again once the bugs are ironed out.

I am a software engineer with severe ADHD (not that unusual in my profession).  I love those times when I "get in the zone" while developing software, though due to my ADHD they are not as often as I would like.  Enter Focus@will.  I have always used music in the past to help me concentrate.  But it wasn't always effective, either due to radio commercials, hearing the same song over again from my own collection, or some other thing.  With focus@will, and the research done by the company behind the app, I now have access to music specifically selected for the ability to help with concentration, without any interruptions. IT REALLY WORKS!  It is worth every cent, and then some.  I really like the research behind the app and how it helps me get in the zone much more often.  Because of that, the app, and the service behind it (you can also use a desktop web browser), this is the most valuable app and service I have purchased!

There were initial problems with earlier versions of the app, but the latest works great with my iPhone 4s.  (The 9+ rating assigned the app for mild language, violence, etc. is absurd!) 

Even if you don't get the app, try their website.  Regardless, it is great music, especially if you like instrumental, classical, or similar music.

I've enjoyed using this app for some time now but this latest version has issues. Basically after one or two songs the audio just stops but it shows to be playing and it shows no indication  that it is buffering or having other network issues. The only way to get it to play another song is to tap the stop button and then tap the play button, which starts out on a new song and breaks my concentration. I would have happily sent them feedback instead of a negative review but the app doesn't have a feedback form.
Would be five stars if it worked

Great little app - already seeing an improvement in my ability to focus. Only complaint is that it stops playing after about 40 minutes (when I've selected it for 60). This disruption breaks my focus a bit because I have to restart the session.

title.label: Desperately needs to automatically pause when headphones are unplugged

content.label: This is a good start and I understand that preventing users from pausing helps them to stay focused.  But seriously, on mobile, it's just annoying.  When I unplug my headphones, I don't want the music to keep playing. EVER!  Please stop being idealistic and start being practical.  We live in a real world were distractions happen.
In the past i had not been able to listen to music while working but this service actually helps me hone my focus. The soothing music allows for clarity to emerge. Well done!

title.label: Makes it easier to ignore distractions

content.label: When listening to this app at work my concentration is better; I can easily ignore distractions and anxieties that often derail me.

I have always liked music playing in the background while I concentrate.  It was sometimes a distraction because often my mind would tune into a favorite song.  That is not the case with focus@will.  It is just there and I barely notice I am listening, my productivity and ability to stay on task have skyrocketed.  I am a programmer and need to keep the logic channels open and flowing for long amounts of time.  This has helped me access those areas of my brain easily and painlessly.

I have long used study music to help me focus (as my mind tends to focus on a long to-do list). The Ambient track helps me to focus on the subject at hand much better than any of my previous focus music (and my previous music listened to was specifically for studying also-not just random background music).

I was skeptical of the app but I figured to give it a shot. Whether I'm writing, cleaning around the house, reading, or doing admin stuff at work, I get stuff done without as many distractions and with fewer errors and to a higher peak.
I love the music, it's already been great for me, but the app itself crashes sometimes.

I have to sign in every time I use the app?? Come on, guys. This is a lousy effort, as it is clearly just a website wrapped as an app. The authors may not consider design to be important, but such an unprofessional offering detracts from the credibility of the while enterprise.
